key_concepts: Chemical symbols represent elements and may come from English or Latin names
Diatomic elements such as hydrogen, oxygen, and chlorine exist as two-atom molecules
Chemical formulas represent ionic and covalent compounds using symbols and subscripts
A word equation uses chemical names to summarize a reaction
A skeleton equation uses chemical formulas and state symbols but is not balanced
A balanced chemical equation has equal numbers of each atom on both sides
The inspection method balances equations by adjusting coefficients
In a chemical equation, reactants are on the left, products on the right, and the arrow me
State symbols (s), (l), (g), and (aq) indicate solid, liquid, gas, and aqueous substances
Chemical changes and chemical reactions are represented by chemical equations
Carbon burns in excess oxygen to form carbon dioxide and in limited oxygen to form carbon
Hydrolysis of calcium carbide produces ethyne gas and calcium hydroxide
